subject: Vocabulary
topic: Antonyms — Advanced SSC CGL Tier 2 Set (W11 B1)

questions.explanation: C is correct. LOQUACIOUS = tending to talk a great deal; talkative. Antonym = RETICENT = not revealing one's thoughts or feelings readily; quiet/reserved. Trap: Talkative (A) = synonym; Verbose (B) = synonym (using more words than needed); Garrulous (D) = synonym (excessively talkative). All three options are synonyms — reticent is the only antonym.

C is correct. MAGNANIMOUS = very generous, forgiving, or noble in spirit. Antonym = PETTY = small-minded, ungenerous, or concerned with trivial matters. Root: 'magnus' (great) + 'animus' (soul) = great-souled. Trap: Generous (A), Noble (B), Benevolent (D) are all synonyms of magnanimous. Only Petty is the antonym.

D is correct. INDOLENT = avoiding activity or exertion; habitually lazy. Antonym = INDUSTRIOUS = hard-working, diligent. Trap: Slothful (A), Torpid (B), Lethargic (C) are all synonyms of indolent (all mean lazy/slow). SSC often packs the options with synonyms to trick students who don't know the word's antonym clearly.

B is correct. PROFLIGATE = recklessly extravagant or wasteful in the use of resources; also, licentious. Antonym = THRIFTY = using money and other resources carefully and not wastefully. Trap: Dissipated (A), Dissolute (C), Debauched (D) are all synonyms of profligate's second meaning (immoral/licentious). Only Thrifty opposes the extravagance meaning.

C is correct. TRUCULENT = eager or quick to argue or fight; aggressively defiant. Antonym = PLACID = not easily upset or excited; calm and peaceful. Trap: Belligerent (A), Aggressive (B), Combative (D) are all synonyms of truculent. Only Placid (calm, peaceable) is the antonym.

C is correct. RECONDITE = not known by many people; obscure, abstruse. Antonym = MANIFEST = clear or obvious to the eye or mind. Root: 'reconditus' = hidden away (Latin). Trap: Esoteric (A), Abstruse (B), Arcane (D) are all synonyms of recondite (all mean obscure/little-known). Manifest is the only antonym (= openly known/obvious).

C is correct. EBULLIENT = cheerful and full of energy; exuberant. Antonym = DESPONDENT = in low spirits from loss of hope or courage; dejected. Trap: Exuberant (A), Vivacious (B), Effervescent (D) are all synonyms of ebullient (high-energy, enthusiastic). Despondent (gloomy, hopeless) is the clear antonym.

C is correct. PARSIMONIOUS = unwilling to spend money or use resources; extremely frugal. Antonym = MUNIFICENT = larger in amount than is necessary or expected; very generous. Trap: Miserly (A), Niggardly (B), Penurious (D) are all synonyms of parsimonious (all mean stingy/mean with money). Munificent (lavishly generous) is the antonym.

C is correct. DIFFIDENT = modest or shy, especially because of a lack of self-confidence. Antonym = ASSERTIVE = having or showing a confident and forceful personality. Trap: Timid (A), Bashful (B), Meek (D) are all synonyms of diffident (all suggest shyness/lack of confidence). Assertive (confident, self-assured) is the antonym.

B is correct. GARRULOUS = excessively talkative, especially on trivial matters. Antonym = LACONIC = using very few words; brief and concise. Root of laconic: Laconians (Spartans) were famous for speaking briefly. Trap: Verbose (A), Loquacious (C), Voluble (D) are all synonyms of garrulous (all mean talkative). Laconic (brief/terse) is the antonym.
